A single old record can outlive retention.ms on disk if it shares a segment with newer records.
The dirty ratio exists specifically to bound how often the cleaner re-copies a log, not to decide which records survive.
A record past the maximum compaction lag is forced eligible even if the dirty ratio hasn't crossed its threshold.

items.item: Tombstone visibility is a race between how fast a consumer catches up and the tombstone's own retention window, not a guarantee independent of consumer speed.
Compaction never reorders records; it only removes superseded ones, so relative order among survivors is preserved.
Ordering within a partition, and what compaction does or doesn't disturb about it, is this topic's own successor topic's job, not retaught here.
A compacted topic's own offset topic (from the previous topic) is itself an example of the compaction mechanics this topic teaches.
